changes.summary: New Playoff Odds page: every team's chance to make the playoffs (and earn a bye), plus the games this week that move it most.
The Saturday Matchup Preview is now chart-led: a playoff race board up top, then a card per game with the rivalry, last five weeks, what's at stake and the schedule left.
The standings Playoffs tab now shows each team's playoff odds on its seed tile, with Odds and Bye columns in the table.
Saturday's group chat lineup check now names every team with no lineup, an empty slot or an OUT/IR/bye starter. Sunday reminders are push only.

Ask the History can now count across the whole record: most trades in a single day, most waiver pickups in a week, who has traded the most.
The trade deadline now follows the Constitution, the Friday before Week 11 at 8:45pm PT, everywhere on the site instead of a fixed Nov 13.
Sorting a roster by a future salary year now switches the cap totals, Cap Subtotals card and cap space (header and phone card) to that year, labeled with it.
Live scoring's matchup detail now shows each team's and player's original projection once games start, so you can see how far off it was.

Free team logo maker at mfl.football/team-logo: pick a style and colors, paste the prompt into ChatGPT or Gemini, then turn the PNG into a sharp SVG. No account needed.

Every Schefter column now reads in short one- or two-sentence paragraphs, so articles are easier to follow on a phone.

Schefter now writes one weekly preview on Saturday instead of two: the Friday Weekend Preview is folded into the Saturday Matchup Preview.

Every game in Schefter's Saturday Matchup Preview now names its key NFL game: the one with the most projected points from both lineups.

Schefter stops reporting trade offers once the trade deadline passes, and skips offers built around a player who has since been traded.
Vegas Vic and Doc Rivers get real cartoon avatars in the news feed, replacing their placeholder badges.
Meet Max Insider, the league's new AI beat reporter: big trades, bids and IR moves get their own posts, and the rest of the wire lands in one daily notebook.
Matchup Preview cards show each team's logo whole instead of cropping it to a circle, and spell out the full team name whenever it fits.
On phones, the homepage's Breaking news card now shows the player above the story, so the headline never covers his face.
The trade deadline countdown now runs to the exact time MFL closes trading, read from MFL's own calendar, instead of midnight.
Top Players drops its Pos column, since the # column already shows the positional rank; the Overall view shows it under each name (RB12).
Every game in the Saturday Matchup Preview now ends with a predicted final score, not just a winner.
Rosters: the Year picker's arrow now has room on its right instead of sitting flush against the edge.
New guide: how the schedule is made, from the rules it follows in order to when it drops each year.
New guide: how the AFL schedule is made, from the Week 1 crossover to the rules it follows and when it drops each year.
File your veteran extension on the League Planner: pick any eligible player, choose +1 or +2 years, see each year's salary, and it goes straight onto MFL.
Rosters: your simulated tags, extensions, 1st-round options and cuts now save to your account, and Review & submit files them all in one go.
Schefter now reports every extension, option and franchise tag with the old and new terms, and leaks tag rumors during the Feb 1-14 window.
Dark mode gets a black top bar, calmer steel blues, and one matching sage green for the league name everywhere.
Schefter's trade posts now name each player once ("WR, Deebo Samuel"), show who got what the right way, and print his take's label only once.
Doc Rivers is back: injury updates for rostered players now post again, and his and Vegas Vic's posts show in the league's main news feed.
Ask the History answers now come from Buck Archives, the league historian, with his name and portrait on every answer.
Buck's Notebook: every Tuesday, Buck Archives posts a few history facts about the coming week, like the week's highest score ever.
